back: Planning, organising, directing and controlling resources to achieve the objectives of a business.
Planning, organising, directing (leading) and controlling; Fayol's list also names commanding and coordinating.
Comparing actual results with plans and taking corrective action.
Interpersonal (figurehead, leader, liaison); informational (monitor, disseminator, spokesperson); decisional (entrepreneur, disturbance handler, resource allocator, negotiator).
Functions say what managers are responsible for (Fayol); roles describe the varied work done in a busy day (Mintzberg).
Taylor: find the one best way by time and motion study; pay for output. Suits repetitive work.
Fayol: management principles and functions apply to all organisations; clear structure but may be rigid.
Weber: rules, clear hierarchy, written records, jobs by qualification; fair and consistent but slow and impersonal.
Mayo and others: social needs, groups and communication matter; raises morale but can be slow.
